titulo: PAU 2027 · Galicia · Lengua Extranjera II: Inglés
instrucciones: The exam lasts 90 minutes and is worth 10 points. It comprises four questions. Answer all the subsections in Questions 1, 2 and 3. In Question 4, answer only ONE of the two options. Write your answers in English. In Question 1.1, copy evidence from the text for True and False answers; no quotation is required for Not Given answers.

preguntas.enunciado:
Read the following text:

Across the region, repair cafés have become a practical way for people to give broken household objects a second life. These community events take place in a range of neighbourhood venues, including school halls and community centres, as well as some public libraries. Visitors bring an item and, with help from a volunteer, try to mend it themselves. The volunteer does not simply take the object away to fix it later: the aim is to help visitors learn how things work.

Lamps, small kitchen appliances and radios are among the most common items brought to sessions. Some cafés also welcome bicycles and clothes. Before any electrical item is opened, a trained volunteer checks that it can be handled safely. If an object cannot be repaired safely, or the necessary parts are unavailable, visitors are advised not to use it.

There is no compulsory fee. Donations are welcome, but they are optional, and the local authority may provide a room or help publicise an event. Organisers say that people often come because they want to avoid buying a replacement. However, they also report that visitors return to practise new skills and meet people in their neighbourhood. The service is not intended to replace professional repair businesses; instead, it helps residents make informed decisions about everyday objects.

By keeping usable goods in circulation, repair cafés aim to reduce waste. Their organisers hope that visitors will share what they learn with friends and family, too. Although the events are becoming more popular, no local survey has yet measured how many extra years a repaired household appliance remains in use.

1.1. After reading the text, indicate whether the following statements are True (T), False (F) or the information is Not Given (NG). In True and False cases only, copy the part of the text which justifies your answer. (1.5 points; 0.25 points each)
1. Every repair café session in the region is held in a public library.
2. Visitors are encouraged to carry out repairs with a volunteer’s help.
3. People have to pay a fixed fee to take part in a session.
4. Some repair cafés accept bicycles and clothes.
5. A local survey found that repaired appliances remain in use for four extra years on average.
6. Organisers say that visitors come only to save money.

1.2. Find a synonym (S) or an antonym (A) in the text for each of the following words. (1 point; 0.2 points each)
1. fix (S)  2. purchase (S)  3. usual (S)  4. compulsory (A)  5. increase (A)
preguntas.solucion:
### 1.1. Comprensión del texto

1. **F (False).** No todas las sesiones se celebran en bibliotecas: el texto menciona distintos lugares. Justificación: “These community events take place in a range of neighbourhood venues, including school halls and community centres, as well as some public libraries.”
2. **T (True).** Los visitantes intentan reparar el objeto con ayuda de una persona voluntaria. Justificación: “Visitors bring an item and, with help from a volunteer, try to mend it themselves.”
3. **F (False).** No hay una tarifa obligatoria; las donaciones son opcionales. Justificación: “There is no compulsory fee. Donations are welcome, but they are optional”.
4. **T (True).** Algunos cafés aceptan bicicletas y ropa. Justificación: “Some cafés also welcome bicycles and clothes.”
5. **F (False).** El texto dice expresamente que ninguna encuesta local ha medido cuántos años adicionales permanece en uso un electrodoméstico reparado. Justificación: “no local survey has yet measured how many extra years a repaired household appliance remains in use.”
6. **F (False).** Evitar comprar un reemplazo es una razón frecuente, pero no la única: también vuelven para practicar habilidades y conocer gente. Justificación: “Organisers say that people often come because they want to avoid buying a replacement. However, they also report that visitors return to practise new skills and meet people in their neighbourhood.”

### 1.2. Sinónimos y antónimos

1. **fix (S):** mend.
2. **purchase (S):** buying.
3. **usual (S):** common.
4. **compulsory (A):** optional.
5. **increase (A):** reduce.
preguntas.resultado: 1.1: 1 F; 2 T; 3 F; 4 T; 5 F; 6 F. 1.2: 1 mend; 2 buying; 3 common; 4 optional; 5 reduce.
preguntas.criterios: Total: 2,5 puntos. Apartado 1.1: 1,5 puntos, a razón de 0,25 por cada enunciado; para las respuestas T/F se requiere también copiar una cita pertinente que justifique la clasificación. En NG no se exige cita. Apartado 1.2: 1 punto, a razón de 0,2 por cada sinónimo o antónimo correcto.

preguntas.enunciado:
Answer the two subsections in this question.

2.1. Write a NEW sentence that has the same meaning as the given one. Use the word or expression in brackets. Do not change the word in brackets. (1.5 points; 0.25 points each)
1. The council opened the new cycle workshop in September. (was)
2. “I will send you the route map tomorrow,” Ana said to Ben. (would)
3. I began volunteering at the centre exactly four years ago, and I still volunteer there. (for)
4. The pavement was so narrow that two wheelchairs could not pass at the same time. (too)
5. People expect the new footbridge to open in June. (expected)
6. Although the organisers faced heavy rain, they held the event outdoors. (despite)

2.2. Answer the following questions about pronunciation. Use standard British English. (1 point; 0.25 points each)
1. Which pair of words is pronounced the same? site/sight, though/through, loose/lose, wear/were, quiet/quite.
2. In which word does the stress fall on the third syllable? volunteer, efficient, bicycle, community.
3. Which two words end in /t/, like the -ed ending in worked? designed, packed, repaired, reached, needed.
4. In which word is the letter g pronounced /g/, as in garden? giant, fragile, energy, engineer, give.
preguntas.solucion:
## 2.1. Transformaciones

Se identifica en cada caso la operación gramatical necesaria y se comprueba que se mantiene el significado y se conserva sin cambios la palabra indicada.

1. **The council opened the new cycle workshop in September. (was)**
   - Se pasa de activa a pasiva: el objeto *the new cycle workshop* pasa a ser sujeto y el pasado simple se transforma en *was + participio pasado*.
   - **The new cycle workshop was opened by the council in September.**

2. **I will send you the route map tomorrow, Ana said to Ben. (would)**
   - Se transforma el estilo directo en indirecto: *will* pasa a *would*, *I* se refiere a Ana, *you* a Ben y *tomorrow* a *the next day*.
   - **Ana told Ben that she would send him the route map the next day.**

3. **I began volunteering at the centre exactly four years ago, and I still volunteer there. (for)**
   - La acción comenzó en el pasado y continúa en el presente; se expresa con presente perfecto continuo y el periodo introducido por *for*.
   - **I have been volunteering at the centre for exactly four years.**

4. **The pavement was so narrow that two wheelchairs could not pass at the same time. (too)**
   - Se sustituye *so + adjetivo + that* por *too + adjetivo + for + complemento + infinitivo*.
   - **The pavement was too narrow for two wheelchairs to pass at the same time.**

5. **People expect the new footbridge to open in June. (expected)**
   - Se usa la pasiva impersonal de *expect*: el elemento esperado pasa a sujeto y se mantiene el infinitivo.
   - **The new footbridge is expected to open in June.**

6. **Although the organisers faced heavy rain, they held the event outdoors. (despite)**
   - Se sustituye la subordinada con *although* por una construcción con *despite* y gerundio.
   - **Despite facing heavy rain, the organisers held the event outdoors.**

## 2.2. Pronunciación (inglés británico estándar)

1. **site/sight**: ambas se pronuncian /saɪt/.
2. **volunteer**: el acento principal cae en la tercera sílaba: /ˌvɒl.ənˈtɪə/.
3. **packed** y **reached**: sus terminaciones *-ed* se pronuncian /t/, como en *worked*.
4. **give**: la letra *g* se pronuncia /g/, /ɡɪv/.

## Comprobación final

Las seis oraciones reformuladas conservan el significado y contienen exactamente la palabra indicada entre paréntesis. En pronunciación, *site/sight* son homófonas; *volunteer* lleva el acento principal en la tercera sílaba; *packed* y *reached* terminan en /t/; y la *g* de *give* es /g/. La puntuación máxima es **2,5 puntos**.
preguntas.resultado: 2.1: 1) The new cycle workshop was opened by the council in September. 2) Ana told Ben that she would send him the route map the next day. 3) I have been volunteering at the centre for exactly four years. 4) The pavement was too narrow for two wheelchairs to pass at the same time. 5) The new footbridge is expected to open in June. 6) Despite facing heavy rain, the organisers held the event outdoors. 2.2: 1) site/sight. 2) volunteer. 3) packed, reached. 4) give.
preguntas.criterios: 2.1: 0,25 puntos por cada una de las seis reformulaciones (1,5 puntos). Se valora que se mantengan el significado y la palabra indicada, además de la corrección gramatical. 2.2: 0,25 puntos por cada respuesta correcta (1 punto). Total: 2,5 puntos. Se aceptan variantes equivalentes y gramaticalmente correctas en 2.1 que respeten la palabra obligatoria y el significado original.

preguntas.enunciado:
In this text, fill each gap with a word or expression from the box below. There are five extra options which you must leave out. Each option may be used only once. (2 points; 0.25 points each)

In the northern district, a youth centre has opened a tool library, 1. __________ residents can borrow equipment instead of buying it. Before the first opening day, volunteers tested every item 2. __________ safety and prepared a simple guide. Members may borrow a drill for 3. __________ seven days, then bring it back 4. __________ the front desk. Any tool that develops a fault is repaired 5. __________ it is lent to another person. Beginners can ask a volunteer to explain 6. __________ to use the equipment safely. The service has attracted many families 7. __________ borrowing is free for registered members. The centre plans to add sewing machines 8. __________ the autumn.

although · because · before · between · despite · for · how · in · unless · to · up to · where · whose
preguntas.solucion:
1. **where**: introduce una oración de relativo que indica el lugar donde los residentes pueden pedir prestado el equipo.
2. **for**: la expresión *test something for safety* significa comprobar que algo es seguro.
3. **up to**: indica el límite máximo de siete días.
4. **to**: expresa el destino al que se devuelve la herramienta.
5. **before**: indica que la reparación se realiza antes de prestar la herramienta a otra persona.
6. **how**: la estructura *explain how to use* significa explicar cómo utilizar algo.
7. **because**: introduce la razón por la que el servicio ha atraído a muchas familias.
8. **in**: se emplea en la expresión temporal *in the autumn*.

**Texto completo:** In the northern district, a youth centre has opened a tool library, **where** residents can borrow equipment instead of buying it. Before the first opening day, volunteers tested every item **for** safety and prepared a simple guide. Members may borrow a drill for **up to** seven days, then bring it back **to** the front desk. Any tool that develops a fault is repaired **before** it is lent to another person. Beginners can ask a volunteer to explain **how** to use the equipment safely. The service has attracted many families **because** borrowing is free for registered members. The centre plans to add sewing machines **in** the autumn.
preguntas.resultado: 1. where; 2. for; 3. up to; 4. to; 5. before; 6. how; 7. because; 8. in.
preguntas.criterios: 0,25 puntos por cada hueco correctamente completado: 8 huecos × 0,25 = 2 puntos. Se aceptan las opciones exactas del recuadro, sin repetir ninguna; las cinco opciones restantes no se utilizan.

preguntas.enunciado:
Answer ONE of the following options. Write about 140 words. (3 points)

4.1. Your town council is asking local students for suggestions about a safer route to school. Write an email to the council recommending two practical changes and explaining how they would help students with different needs.

4.2. The school e-magazine is publishing a feature on public libraries and young people. Write an opinion article discussing whether libraries should stay open later in the evening for teenagers. Give reasons and examples to support your view.
preguntas.solucion:
### Desarrollo
1. Se elige la opción 4.1 y se adopta el formato de correo formal.
2. Se proponen dos cambios concretos: mejorar los cruces y hacer más accesibles los pavimentos.
3. Se explica cómo cada medida beneficia a estudiantes con necesidades distintas. El modelo tiene aproximadamente 143 palabras.

**Subject: A safer route to school**

Dear Council Members,

I am writing to recommend two changes to make the walk to school safer and more accessible.

First, install traffic lights with audible signals and longer crossing times at busy junctions. Drivers would have to stop, while students with visual impairments could follow the sound cues and wheelchair users or young children would have enough time to cross safely.

Second, improve pavements with street lighting, dropped kerbs and tactile paving, and keep them clear of parked cars. Good lighting would help students walking in winter; accessible pavements would benefit wheelchair users, people with pushchairs and anyone with limited mobility. Tactile paving would also guide students with visual impairments.

These practical measures would make the journey safer for everyone, not only confident walkers. I hope the council will consider them.

Yours faithfully,
A local student
preguntas.resultado: Opción 4.1: correo formal con dos recomendaciones prácticas y nota estimada de 3/3.
preguntas.criterios: Reparto aplicado: 1 punto por responder a la tarea con dos propuestas pertinentes y explicar sus beneficios; 1 punto por organización, cohesión, formato y registro adecuados; 1 punto por corrección y variedad léxica y gramatical. Nota estimada del modelo: 3/3.
